Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary. High level responses inline, then proposed next steps.

1) Deprecation timeline: we are planning a major SDK surface update (v3.0) in Q2 2027; any deprecations that affect v2.x will be announced at least 90 days before removal and we will maintain v2.x security fixes for 12 months after GA of v3.0.

2) Stability/rollback: Redwood can commit to a partner canary window and a fallback policy for partner-tagged traffic. We do not offer a formal SLA on non-dedicated hosted tiers, but for partners we can negotiate an SLA addendum if you move to Dedicated capacity or the partner SLA program (I can propose language).

3) Assisted migration: we can offer a limited-run migration plan that includes a compatibility shim, a runbook for rolling upgrades, and 2 days of dev support for integration testing.

Next steps I suggest:
- I will draft an MA (mutual action plan) and a proposed freeze window (Nov 15 — May 15 for customers who opt into a partner stability track).
- Internal alignment with Markus (program owner's engineering constraints) and Marcus (partner success) to cost out the assisted migration.

I will attach a preliminary timeline and impact matrix.

Best,
Irene

Irene — a few engineering notes on constraints:

- Maintaining v2 security patches for 12 months is doable but requires a branch-maintenance cadence and a small team allocation (approx 0.2 FTE infra/quarter).
- Partner canary: we can tag partner traffic at the router level and provide per-token rollback for impacted endpoints; time to roll back ~2–5 minutes in most cases.
- Compatibility shim: easiest if we provide a thin adapter (JS + Python) that maps v2 client calls to v3 endpoints; non-trivial differences are in streaming token behavior and function-call wiring.

Irene — I'll sketch a minimal tech plan and a rough estimate this afternoon.
